title: Integration On Manifolds
notes: Open by framing integration as the chapter where orientation, maps, and topology begin to talk through numbers. The source span is pages 151 through 201, but the lecture path is operational: choose a form, move it with pullback, differentiate it, integrate it, and read the invariant it reveals.

title: The Chapter Arc
notes: Use the route diagram to keep the lecture from becoming a catalog of operations. Exterior algebra gives the sign discipline, forms attach that algebra to tangent spaces, integration depends on orientation, and Stokes theorem becomes the bridge from local derivative data to global topological information.

title: Exterior Algebra Is A Sign Machine
notes: Slow down on the wedge table because many later mistakes are sign mistakes in disguise. Repeated covectors vanish because a degenerate parallelogram has no oriented area, while swapping the order reverses orientation. The determinant formula is the local ancestor of change of variables.

title: Forms Attach Algebra To Each Tangent Space
notes: Present a differential form as a smoothly varying measuring device rather than as a decorated expression. At each point it eats tangent vectors and returns signed volume, and the smoothness condition ensures those measurements change coherently across charts and overlap regions.

title: Pullback Moves Forms Backward
notes: Stress the contravariant direction. A map sends points and tangent vectors forward, but it lets forms be evaluated on the source by feeding forward the tangent vectors first. This makes integrals computable in source coordinates and packages the Jacobian determinant without separate bookkeeping.

title: Top Forms Are Integrands With Orientation
notes: Integration of a top-degree form is not just area with a positive density. Orientation chooses which ordered bases count positively, so a chart with reversed orientation changes the sign. The partition sketch shows why local chart computations can be added into a global integral.

title: The Exterior Derivative Measures Boundary-Relevant Change
notes: Connect the formula for d omega to the familiar curl pattern without reducing the concept to vector calculus. The exterior derivative raises degree, is independent of the chosen chart, and satisfies d squared equals zero, which will later make exact forms automatically closed.

title: Stokes Theorem Is The Master Conversion
notes: Treat Stokes theorem as a conversion rule between an interior derivative integral and a boundary integral. The disk example is deliberately simple: the rotational one-form has exterior derivative equal to area form, so the boundary circulation equals the area integral with the chosen orientation.

title: Boundary Orientation Carries The Sign
notes: Use this slide as a diagnostic for the most common source of wrong answers. Boundary orientation is not arbitrary decoration; it is induced from the orientation of the manifold. In dimension two the positive boundary direction keeps the region on the left as one walks along the boundary.

title: Closed Need Not Mean Exact
notes: Make the punctured plane example the first genuine topological payoff. The angular form has zero exterior derivative away from the origin, but its period around a loop is nonzero. If it were globally exact, every closed-loop integral would vanish by Stokes, so the hole is detected by the form.

title: Form Cohomology Records Period Obstructions
notes: Explain de Rham cohomology as a ledger of closed forms modulo those that are visibly derivatives. Exact forms integrate to zero on closed cycles, while closed non-exact forms can carry periods. The quotient language records which measurements survive all choices of primitive.

title: Mappings Turn Integrals Into Degree
notes: Relate this slide back to oriented intersection theory from the previous chapter. For compact oriented manifolds of the same dimension, pulling back a top form scales the total integral by the degree. On the circle, theta mapped to m theta makes the ratio visibly equal to m.

title: Change Of Variables Is Pullback Plus Orientation
notes: Separate the analytic and geometric ingredients. The analytic expression is the determinant of the derivative inside the pulled-back top form. The geometric meaning is that the source integral and the target integral agree when orientation is respected, and reverse sign when the chart or map reverses orientation.

title: Gauss-Bonnet Converts Curvature Into Euler Characteristic
notes: Present Gauss-Bonnet as the chapter finale rather than a separate theorem from another course. Curvature is a local two-form on an oriented surface, but its normalized integral returns a topological integer. The sphere and torus budget comparison makes the sign cancellation visible.

title: Notebook Diagnostics As Lecture Evidence
notes: Use the check board to show that the notebook artifacts are not ornamental. Each computation tests one structural claim: wedge signs, determinant scaling, pullback equality, Stokes residual, nonzero period, degree ratio, and Gauss-Bonnet budget. The lecture can point to these as reproducible evidence.

title: Operational Checklist
notes: Close with a procedure students can actually run. Choose the degree and orientation, express the form in a chart, pull back when a map is present, compute exterior derivatives for boundary questions, integrate with the induced orientation, and compare the result with the invariant predicted by Stokes, degree, or Gauss-Bonnet.
